Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Digital revenue collection initiatives exist; the Government launched a Digital Invoicing System via the Gambia Revenue Authority (GRA) for real-time monitoring of sales data and improved tax reporting/collection.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. GRA's Digital Invoicing System (July 2025) supports real-time sales monitoring but is not itself a tax-payment channel; the broader ITAS e-payment module remains in nationwide rollout as of June 2026 (Voice Out Digital, Foroyaa), so only partial digital revenue collection is evidenced. Score unchanged at 2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: GRA launched an Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) described as a web-based platform intended to take tax administration fully online, including taxpayer registration, filing, and making payments through secure digital channels (evidence from public video transcript).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and freshened. Multiple June 2026 reports show GRA's Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) is still being sensitised to taxpayers ahead of a 'full nationwide rollout', with e-filing/e-payment not yet live nationally — consistent with Under development. Replaces the single 2025 YouTube clip with three independent 2026 news sources.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.

revision_notes: Confirmed. Gamswitch/RTGS provide interbank transfer infrastructure capable of business-to-business payments, though no source describes a dedicated, explicitly branded B2B product. Score unchanged at 2 (Yes); evidence remains generic rather than B2B-specific.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Government-to-person payments have been implemented at least for social transfers; the Nafa-Quick emergency cash transfer scheme (COVID response) covered ~83,000 households and used a digital MIS (openIMIS) to manage beneficiary lists and payment processes (article describes digitized management, though disbursement described as cash collection).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded on fresher evidence. Since January 2026, the World Bank-funded Nafa/RISE cash-transfer programme disburses bi-monthly grants to 15,000+ rural households cashlessly via the Wave mobile-money platform, with further urban E-money rollout confirmed in June 2026 — superseding the 2021 evidence of cash handouts with only digital record-keeping (openIMIS). This is active, not merely limited, G2P digital payment use.

Comments: Person-to-government payments are being digitized for government services: Government of The Gambia partnered with Yonna Wallet so that government fees (rates, business registration, ID cards, passports, and other service fees) can be paid via Yonna Wallet app.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: The Consumer Protection Act 2014 provides consumer rights relevant to payments, including ability to request cancellation of credit card payments where fraudulent use is made and requirement that consumers be re-credited, supporting a payments consumer protection framework.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a stronger, payment-specific source. The Central Bank's Regulation on Retail Transfers (issued under the Electronic Payments System Act 2013) contains a dedicated Section 11 'Consumer Protection' setting disclosure, transaction-notification and liability rules for payment service providers — more directly on-point than the general 2014 Consumer Protection Act originally cited. Score unchanged at 3 (Yes).

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 includes mandatory breach notification: controllers must notify the Commission within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach and notify affected data subjects without undue delay where high risk exists.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed by three independent legal-tracker sources: the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 (assented 7 November 2025) requires notification to the Information Commission within 72 hours and to affected data subjects without undue delay for high-risk breaches, with criminal penalties for concealment. Score unchanged at 3 (Mandatory).

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Evidence of pro-poor governance mechanisms is limited; however, CBG's National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) includes a Financial Literacy and Consumer Protection Working Group mandated to provide redress mechanisms for users, particularly women and youth, and to review consumer protection guidelines in digital finance context.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a second AFI source. CBG's National Financial Inclusion Strategy includes a Financial Literacy and Consumer Protection Working Group and a Gender-Sensitive Consumer Protection Framework targeting women and youth, but this sits within broader financial-inclusion governance rather than dedicated instant-payment-system governance. Score unchanged at 2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: BANTABA 2.0 (Gambia's first inclusive instant payment system) was officially launched in Dec 2025 as a national interoperable payments platform enabling real-time digital payments between banks and mobile money providers, built on Mojaloop and operated by Gamswitch (the national payment switch).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed by four independent sources (press release, Mojaloop Foundation, IIDiA, Gamswitch) describing BANTABA 2.0's live launch on 15 December 2025, connecting banks, mobile money operators and fintechs for over 3 million Gambians, with 'full national adoption planned in subsequent phases' — consistent with Partially deployed rather than Fully deployed nationwide. Score unchanged at 4.
